<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par133 />of a ''separation, distinction'' or ''superiority'' of one person or thing ''from'' or ''over'' others.<ref>Cf. the Latin ablative with the comparative; also the etymology of such words as ''eximius, egregius'', and the Homeric ἐκ πάντων μάλιστα, Il. 4, 96; ἐκ πασέων, 18, 431.</ref> This is evident in such cases as {{GHGheb|text=בָּחַר מִן־|translate=to choose}} something (to prefer it) ''before'' something else, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=7|verse=15}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=14|verse=2}} (also {{GHGheb|text=יִתְרוֹן... מִן־|translate=the excellence of... over...}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=2|verse=13}}); it is also seen in examples like {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=37|verse=3}} {{GHGheb|text=וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אָהַב אֶת־יוֹסֵף מִכָּל־בָּנָיו|translate=now Israel loved Joseph more than all his}} (other) ''children''; 29:30, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=6|verse=6}}.<ref>On the other hand, the phrase {{GHGheb|text=צָדַק מִן־}} expresses not a comparison, but only a relation existing between one person and another; thus, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=צָֽדְקָה מִמֶּ֫נִּי}} means, ''she is in the right as against me''; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=32|verse=2|hidebook=1}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=17|verse=12}} ''rather'' (to meet with so and so) ''than''... is expressed by {{GHGheb|text=וְאַל־}} before the second member.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|c}}
2. A somewhat different idea underlies the use of {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} after adjectives, or intransitive verbs possessing an attributive sense, when the thought to be expressed is that the quality is ''too little'' or ''too much'' in force for the attainment of a particular aim or object, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=הַמְעַט מִכֶּם|translate=is it a small thing}} (i.e. too little) ''for you to...?'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=11}}; after an intransitive verb, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=11}} ''I am too insignificant'' ({{GHGheb|text=קָטֹ֫נְתִּי}}) ''for all the mercies'' (I am not worthy of...), &c.; cf. also the expressions {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד מִן־|translate=to be too heavy for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=18|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=5}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָשָׁה מִן־|translate=to be too hard for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=מָעַט מִן־|translate=to be too few for something}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=גָּבַר מִן־|translate=to be too strong for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=עָצַם מִן־|translate=to be too mighty for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=26|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=רוּם מִן־|translate=to be too high for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=61|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=צַר מִן־|translate=to be too narrow for one}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָצַר מִן־|translate=to be too short for something}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=2}}, and very frequently {{GHGheb|text=נִפְלָא מִן־|translate=to be too wonderful for one}} (and, consequently, inconceivable or unattainable), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=17|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=30|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=18}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=139|verse=6}} {{GHGheb|text=פְּלִיאָה}} in the same sense is followed by {{GHGheb|text=מִן}}.—This use is especially seen in the numerous instances in which the attribute is followed by {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} with an infinitive, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=64}} ''the brazen altar... was'' {{GHGheb|text=קָטֹן מֵֽהָכִיל|translate=too little to receive}} (to be able to receive) ''the burnt offering'', cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=4|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=36|verse=7|hidebook=1}} ''too great for them to dwell together''; after verbs, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=40|verse=6}}. Finally, cf. {{GHGheb|text=רַב לָכֶם מִן־}}, followed by the infinitive, ''it is enough'' (prop. ''too much'') ''for you to...'', meaning ''ye have... long enough'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=12|verse=28}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=9|verse=28}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=6}} ({{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} followed by a substantive).<ref>Cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=4|verse=3}}, where the idea of ''doing something too little'' is paraphrased by the Hiph. {{GHGheb|text=הִמְעִיט}} = ''do not too little'', sc. {{GHGheb|text=לִשְׁאֹל|translate=in borrowing}} empty vessels.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|d}}
In all these instances {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} expresses either the ''removal'' of a thing ''from'' a person, or the ''severance'' of the person from some aim or object; cf. also the expression {{GHGheb|text=לֹֽא־יִבָּצֵר מֵהֶם כֹּל וגו׳|translate=nothing will be unattainable for them}} (prop. there shall not be cut off from them anything which, &c.), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=11|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=3}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|133|e}}
3. The attributive idea, on which {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} logically depends, must sometimes, in consequence of a pregnant use of the {{GHGheb|text=מִן־}} (see the analogous examples in {{GHGpar|119|ff}}), be supplied from the context, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=וּפְסִֽלֵיהֶם מִירֽוּשָׁלַ֫יִם|translate=whose graven images}} were more numerous ''than'' those at ''Jerusalem'', &c.;<ref>With this ''comparatio decurtata'', cf. the still bolder pregnant construction in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=4|verse=8}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵעֵת|translate=greater gladness than at the time}}, &c.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=4}} worse ''than a thorn hedge''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=62|verse=10}} lighter ''than a breath''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=11|verse=17}} clearer ''than the noonday''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=4|verse=17}} better ''than'', &c.<section end=par133 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
